paper.title: From Procedural Skills to Strategy Genes: Towards Experience-Driven Test-Time Evolution
paper.central_claim: Reusable experience should be encoded as a compact, control-oriented Strategy Gene under the Gene Evolution Protocol rather than a documentation-style Skill package; Gene gives better test-time control (54.0 vs 51.0 no guidance vs 49.9 Skill over 45 scenarios) and is a better carrier for iterative experience accumulation, with gene-evolved agents improving CritPt from 9.1% to 18.57% and 17.7% to 27.14%.

evidence.quote:
This beta technical report asks how reusable experience should be represented so that it can function as effective test-time control and as a substrate for iterative evolution.
We study this question in 4,590 controlled trials across 45 scientific code-solving scenarios. We find that documentation-oriented Skill packages provide unstable control: their useful signal is sparse, and expanding a compact experience object into a fuller documentation package often fails to help and can degrade the overall average.
We further show that representation itself is a first-order factor.
A compact Gene representation yields the strongest overall average, remains competitive under substantial structural perturbations, and outperforms matched-budget Skill fragments, while reattaching documentation-oriented material usually weakens rather than improves it.
Beyond one-shot control, we show that Gene is also a better carrier for iterative experience accumulation: attached failure history is more effective in Gene than in Skill or freeform text, editable structure matters beyond content alone, and failure information is most useful when distilled into compact warnings rather than naively appended.
On CritPt, gene-evolved systems improve over their paired base models from 9.1% to 18.57% and from 17.7% to 27.14%.
These results suggest that the core problem in experience reuse is not how to supply more experience, but how to encode experience as a compact, control-oriented, evolution-ready object.
evidence.support_explanation: 作者原中心主张与实验规模；包含表征、累积及 CritPt 三层主张，不能只保留一击收益。

evidence.quote:
This structure differs from procedural skills in both organization and purpose.
Skills organize experience according to documentation logic; genes organize experience according to control logic.
Skills prioritize readability and completeness; genes prioritize signal density, applicability boundaries, and failure salience.
The intended use is therefore different as well: a procedural skill is primarily a documentation artifact, whereas a strategy gene is a model-facing control representation.

This distinction also explains why genes require protocolization.
Without a protocol layer, a gene remains a free-form prompt fragment whose boundaries are unstable and whose internal fields are difficult to compare, manipulate, or accumulate systematically.
We therefore introduce the
Gene Evolution Protocol
(GEP) as a representation interface that canonicalizes genes into structured objects:
evidence.support_explanation: 改变经验表示目的及 canonicalization 接口。

evidence.quote:
Canonicalization through GEP serves three purposes.
First, it provides stable boundaries and internal structure, making genes explicit objects rather than ad hoc text snippets.
Second, it makes genes comparable and operable: once protocolized, genes can be matched, replaced, revised, and composed at the object level.
Third, it provides the minimal interface required for accumulation and evolution, so that experience units can be inherited, corrected, validated, and iteratively refined over time.
In this sense, GEP is not a formatting detail, but the protocol layer that lifts a control-oriented representation into an evolution-ready experience object.
evidence.support_explanation: 作者给出可替换、修订、组合与迭代的设计理由；不等于实际闭环效应。

evidence.quote:
Within this setting, Evolver acts as a structured evolution engine rather than a free-form prompting layer.
It selects or updates genes based on runtime signals, constrains candidate modifications through explicit strategy fields, and requires validation before successful experience is solidified.
As a result, the evolved agent does not simply “remember more” in a loose sense.
Instead, it gradually accumulates compact procedures that can be reinvoked in later runs.

The mechanism (control density, structured editability) yields distinguishable predictions (matched-budget fragments, flattening), but the load-bearing operation — distilling a gene from skills/trajectories — is specified only as an abstract map ψ (opus:O05), so authoring quality/effort could carry the effect; perturbation results where stale or overconstrained genes beat the clean gene (opus:O04) and keywords-only ≈ full gene cut against the stated representation mechanism; the evolution story (Evolver/GEP) is not tied to any mechanism test. Key assumptions remain weak (anchor 2).

X.reason: Both seats 2; verified. Gene schema and the GEP scan→signal→intent→mutate→validate→solidify loop are described at protocol level and probe prompts are shown; gene construction, validation thresholds, admission/rejection counts, rollback/retirement and the CritPt setup are not reconstructable.

E.measurement.reason: Resolved to son55's 2. Sandboxed checkpoint pass rate is objective and both models are reported separately, but the 45-scenario benchmark and its test scripts are in-house and unaudited, genes encode exactly the scenario failure modes that the checkpoints test, and the CritPt headline compares the authors' own agent runs against base-model numbers taken from elsewhere — the two sides of the headline are not measured under one protocol. sol's 3 did not weigh the CritPt measurement mismatch.

E.causality.reason: Both seats 2; verified. Token-matched fragments (opus:O06), content/structure perturbations and flattening give partial attribution on this benchmark; authoring effort is not matched, there is no gene-off/store-off control in the same runtime for Evolver, external arXiv genes dominate Version B (opus:O09), and noise is not separated from deltas.

E.holdout.reason: Both seats 1; verified. Experience is distilled per scenario and tested on the same scenario (no construction/test split); evolution tasks, arXiv-derived genes and CritPt are not shown disjoint; claims generalise from one in-house benchmark and one model family.

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 1; verified under A2. Totals (4,590 'retained' trials, opus:O08) and negative cells are reported, but no per-cell repeats, intervals or tests; the identical no-guidance condition moves 2.2 pp on Pro between tables (opus:O01 vs O02), the same size as the headline +3.0 average, whose gain is entirely on Flash (opus:O03); excluded trials are unaccounted.

E.cost.reason: Resolved to son55's 2. For the one-shot representation claim, prompt budgets are explicit (≈230 vs ≈2,500 tokens) and a matched-budget fragment control is run (opus:O06) — budget fairness is directly addressed, not merely mentioned; an end-to-end cost is reported for one CritPt run. Key gaps: that cost is I/O-only (opus:O07) and the two-day evolution, gene mining and failed trials are uncosted, so not 3. sol's 1 discounted the matched-budget control as 'local prompt budget'.

resolutions.reason: The paper's stated point of departure is to test the assumption that more complete, structured experience representations are better and to pivot to a compact representation; the probes are the instrument. Primary assumption_audit_and_pivot (no sub fits).

Keep son55's primary, sol's C02 for the confound-isolating probes (length/structure/content varied with template fixed), and adapt_via_conditioning for the deployment channel (gene injected into a frozen model's systemInstruction). son55's architectural_operator_substitution is dropped: the surrogate is not shown to preserve a property by construction and the motive is control, not compute.

H02 (package vs compact object) is common to both. H01 (curate a living store with edit operations) fits the GEP mutate/validate/solidify loop better than sol's H00 (reflect into lessons). sol's H32 is kept for the controlled representation probes. son55's H30 is dropped: GEP's gate has no measured admission/retirement test (its own F1 'infrastructure offered as the gate'), so it is recorded as a failed condition check, not a member match.
